segments.text: This is Aakashwani, I am Valsa Williams with the news at 9.
The headlines Government approved schemes to make the country
a global manufacturing hub of containers and sports goods also gives the nod to Pradhan
Mantri Vikasit Gram Swaraj Yojna to strengthen grassroots governance.
BJP NDA sweeps Karnataka Legislative Council elections, counting continues for MLC polls
in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra.
Heavy rain batters northern and under Pradesh and southern Odisha as cyclone or knob weakens
after landfall, leaving trail of destruction.
Ministry of External Affairs says 22 Indian nationals, including 14 seafarers killed in
West Asia conflict so far, reiterates India's firm stand against terror financing and cross-border
terrorism amid ongoing FATF meeting in Paris.
Two high-speed trains collided in Toledo, province of Spain, killing 68 people.
And Indian women shine in sports, Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Dhochak win silver medals at world
wrestling championships, cricket team, clean sweeps, three-match ODI series against Zimbabwe.
The government today approved several key initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic
manufacturing and promoting rural governance.
The decisions were taken at a union cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Briefing near New Delhi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnava announced the details.
Mr Vaishnav said the cabinet has approved the container manufacturing promotion scheme
with a total outlay of 10,000 crore rupees over 13 years up to the financial year 2039-40.
The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India.
Containers are a major fulcrum of trade for India and the world.
The container manufacturing scheme that the prime minister has approved in the cabinet
includes elements that, in the coming few years, India will emerge as a new destination
for container manufacturing. The Cabinet has also given the nod to the Kelo-India Sports
Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods.
This is a long-term scheme for sports goods spanning an eight-year period. It has an
outlay of Rs 1,856.67 crore and will remain operational from fiscal year 2026-27 to fiscal
year 2033-34. It has two pillars. The first pillar consists of incentives to support manufacturing.
The second pillar consists of incentives to develop the entire ecosystem. The Cabinet
also cleared the Pratamantri Vikasit Gram Thvaraj Yojana as a centrally sponsored
scheme with a total financial outlay of 7,395 crore rupees. The scheme will be implemented
over five years from 2026-2027 to 2031 to empower gram panchayats and strengthen grass
roots governance.
The basic thirst of the Prime Minister's Vixit Gram Suraj Yojana is to build capacity
at the local level, identify resources, identify constraints, and carry out planning at the
local level, keeping in view local resources, constraints, and capacity.
This is the main thrust, and it is a major paradigm shift.
In while the Cabinet has also approved a 3% increase in dearness allowance for central
government employees and dearness relief for pensioners, with effect from 1 July this
year.
Counting of votes is underway for Legislative Council elections in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh
and Bihar, while results for all four seats in Karnataka have been declared. Elections
were held for a total of 28 seats across the four states. In Karnataka, the BJP-led
NDA has dominated the Legislative Council elections, with the BJP winning three seats
and its allies and Sadhaal Sekula securing one seat. In Uttar Pradesh, results have
been declared for eight out of 11 Legislative Council seats, with the BJP winning five seats
and the Samajwadi Party securing three. In Bihar, results for six of the eight seats have
been declared, with the BJP winning two seats while the JDU, RJD, Jansu Raj and an independent
candidate have secured one seat each. In Maharashtra, out of a total of five seats,
the BJP and Shiv Sena have so far secured a seat each in the Legislative Council elections.
Pro-Minister Narendra Modi today took a dig at the Congress Party over the MLC elections
held using ballot papers. In a social media post, Mr Modi questioned the Congress Party's
performance asking how many seats it has won in these elections.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News. Follow us on X at AIR News Alerts and visit newsonair.gov.in
for the latest updates. Welcome back here with us on the news at nine. Cyclone
Ornup has weakened into a deep depression after making landfall along
the Andhra Pradesh coast, leaving a trail of a destruction. According to the
Intermetrological Department, IMD, the storm crossed the coast between
Baputla and Vishakapatnam near Narsapur and southwest of Yanom early
this morning. The system is continuing to weaken as it drifts slowly
north westward towards Shatisgarh and Telangana. The weather system is triggering heavy rainfall
across northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha. Relief and rescue operations in the
worst affected regions of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha continue following the landfall
of the cyclone. Over 180,000 people have been evacuated to safer zones and relief shelters
across the two states. The Andhra Pradesh government has announced financial assistance
for families and businesses affected by the cyclone, we have more from our correspondent.
Amravati Meteorological Centre has forecasted heavy rainfall over the next three hours
in several districts of Andhra Pradesh including Srikakulam, Elur, Konisima, East Godavari,
West Godavari, NTR and Guntur.
In the past 12 hours, Vishak Patnam recorded 21 centimeters of rainfall
while Vijayanagara and Srikakulam districts received 14 centimeters each.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrapapnidhu has directed officials to
provide essential commodities to people whose houses have been inundated by the cyclone.
Chief Minister also stated that assistance of Rs.10,000 would be provided for partially
damaged houses and Rs.25,000 for shops affected by the cyclone.
Satya Narayana, Aakashwani News, Vishak Patna.
In Odisha, the IMD has issued a red warning for six districts.
Gangram, Gajapati, Korapur, Navarangapur, Malkan, Keri and Raigada.
Flooding, damage to houses and disruptions to road and rail services remain major concerns.
Chief Minister Mohanjaran Malchi has reviewed the situation, while authorities remain on
high alert.
We have a report.
Cyclone Arnav continues to affect southern Odisha with heavy rainfall and strong winds
disrupting normal life in several areas.
Several houses have reportedly been damaged in Jaipur and Potangi.
4 gates of Harbhangi Dam have been opened and residents of low-lying areas have been
alerted.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan-Maji reviewed the situation this evening in the Special Relief
Commissioner's office.
Rail services have been cancelled or regulated on several routes, while bus connectivity
to southern Odisha has faced precautionary restrictions.
Meanwhile, the IMD has said that another weather system is developing over the south
Andaman Sea.
An upper-air-clinic circulation over the region is likely to trigger the formation
of a low-pressure area within the next 24 hours.
Prakash Das, Akash Vani News, Bhubaneswar.
The cyclone has caused widespread damage in the Yanom region of Puducherry.
Standing paddy crops have been inundated while fishermen have suffered losses as large
stocks of dried fish stored on coastal fish-drying platforms were damaged.
The government has assured people of all necessary assistance.
The IMD has issued an orange-colour warning for very heavy rainfall for Bihar, Chhattisgarh,
East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha tomorrow.
The external affairs ministry has said 22 Indians, including 14 seafarers, have been killed
so far in the ongoing West Asia conflict.
Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, ministry spokesperson Ranthi Jaiswal expressed
deep concern over the ongoing conflict.
We deeply concerned with the ongoing conflict in West Asia.
So far we have lost 22 Indian nationals in the conflict, which includes 14 seafarers.
And on our part we remain in close touch with the community there so that we can do our best
for the safety and well-being.
Speaking about the ongoing financial action task force FATF meeting in Paris, the spokesperson
reiterated India's firm stand against terror financing and cross-border terrorism.
As far as terror financing is concerned or cross-border terrorism is concerned, we have
been amply clear as to where we stand.
These are things that need to be held accountable.
We need to do more so that terrorism in all its forms and manifestations can be fought
harder and defeated by the global community.
External Affairs Minister Dr. S. J. Shankar today held talks with his Austrian counterpart
to strengthen bilateral cooperation and discuss key global issues.
In a social media post, Dr. Jaishankar said they explored new avenues of cooperation
in startups, space, skill development and mobility.
Earlier in the day in his opening remarks,
Dr. Jaishankar said India's ties with the European Union had intensified
and that New Delhi looked forward to the free trade agreement coming into force
in the coming months.
It's natural that India and Austria who have such a warm and friendly relationship that
we would discuss many of those issues and see how we can together contribute to international
peace and security.
Let me take this opportunity to also congratulate you on becoming a non-permanent member of
the United Nations Security Council.
We, again, have a long history of cooperating in the UN framework.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met his Japanese counterpart Koizumi Shinjiro on the sidelines
of the 13th ASEAN Defence Minister's meeting, ADMM+, in the Philippines.
In a social media post, Mr Singh said they held productive discussions on reviewing the
ongoing inter-tropan bilateral defence cooperation.
He noted that the shared commitment of both nations remained vital for a free, open and
peaceful Indo-Pacific region.
Earlier in the day, the Defence Minister met US Secretary of War Pete Hexit and Australian
counterpart and Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marz.
In Spain, 68 people were killed after two high-speed trains collided in Toledo Province.
According to the country's rail infrastructure operator, the collision occurred when a
train operated by Renfe, the state-owned railway company, carrying 397 passengers collided with
the rear of a stationary train, operated by Irio, a private high-speed rail operator,
with 147 passengers on board, on the Madrid-Serville line near the town of Urda.
Spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government, Esther Padilla, said
the cause of the crash was not known, adding that the death toll is likely to rise.
You are listening to the news at 9 on Akash Varni.
In sports Indian women wrestlers Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Thochak clinched silver medals in
the respective categories of the world championships in Astana, Kazakhstan today, 26 year old
Neelam clinched the medal in the women's 50kg category after losing 5-0 to Japanese wrestling
legend Yu-I-Susaki in the final. Kajal also settled for the silver after suffering a narrow
8-6 to Ukraine's Anastasia Alpeyeva in the final of 76kg category. With this achievement,
Neelam and Kajal have joined Anshu Malik as the only Indian women wrestlers to have
won silver medals at the global showpiece. In women's cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe
by eight wickets in the third and final one-day international in Varodhra this evening to sweep
the series 3-0, chasing a target of 132 runs India overhauled the score in 17 overs, losing
two wickets, earlier opting to bat first after winning the toss, Zimbabwe were bolted out for
131 runs in 39.5 overs. And now before we enter the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Government approves schemes to make the country a global manufacturing hub of containers and

governance. BJP NDS sweeps, Karnataka Legislative Council elections counting continues for MNC

than Entrepreneurship Southern Odisha, as Cyclone Ordnop weakens after landfall, Ministry
